study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized cortical thickness asymmetry in Autism Spectrum Disorders and Schizophrenia

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Apply normative modeling to quantify individual-level deviations in cortical thickness asymmetry (AI) in ASD and SZ, and assess whether deviations are over-represented regionally or at whole-brain level compared to healthy controls.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Group comparisons of deviation metrics: chi-square permutation tests with FDR for regional percentage maps (HCtest vs ASD/SZ); comparisons of average number of deviant regions (z-statistics) per individual; whole-brain AI z-score distributions compared between groups; multivariate analysis via t-SNE embedding + k-medoids clustering (no diagnostic separation).
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: ASD cortical thickness asymmetry lies within normative variation at whole-brain and regional levels; SZ shows only a very small, isolated regional difference with minimal effect size; multivariate patterns do not differentiate diagnoses.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: No differences in whole-brain AI z-scores between HCtest and ASD or SZ (P > 0.05). Regionally, only one superior temporal region showed higher supra-normal AI proportion in SZ vs HCtest (HCtest=1.14%, SZ=5.92%, χ2=15.45, PFDR<0.05, ω=0.14). SZ had a higher average number of regions with infra-/supra-normal deviations than HCtest (infra-normal: z=-4.21, p<0.01; supra-normal: z=-4.33, p<0.01). Multivariate clustering of z-scores (t-SNE + k-medoids) showed no association with diagnosis.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Alternative AI computation using FreeSurfer xhemi/qcache; replication with higher-resolution parcellation; site bias assessed via linear SVM on HC z-scores; robustness checks for handedness and IQ.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Within-site split only (no external domain validation); site handled as fixed covariate (no hierarchical random effects or heteroscedastic modeling); normative modeling assumed linear relationships; limited female sample precluded female-only analyses; pooled HC mean/SD ages not reported.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Full dataset list observed in supplement: ABIDE-I NYU; ABIDE-I USM; ABIDE-II GU; ABIDE-II OHSU; MITASD; WASHASD; MADRID-ASD; BGS; COBRE; UTRECHT; AOMIC-ID1000; AOMIC-PIOP1; AOMIC-PIOP2; CAMCAN; DLBS; IXI; NARRATIVES; SALD; OASIS; ROCKLAND. Training set: 4904 HCs (54.85% female), age 6–95. Test set includes HCtest (n=526; ~40% male) and all cases (ASD n=135; SZ n=287). QC: CAT12 IQR>2.8 excluded 682 images; Euler threshold excluded 5 images. Parcellation: 160-region symmetric atlas (Romero-Garcia 2014); alternative A1 uses 1000-region Schaefer atlas; alternative A2 uses xhemi vertex-wise mapping then region-averaged AI.
